## Notes

- [MULTI_STACK] — Two stacks coexist: TypeScript/Next.js application + HCL/Terraform AWS infra (infra/).
- Path alias: `@/*` → repo root (./). Common: `@/lib/*`, `@/components/*`.
- **Auth is MOCK**: `lib/auth/mock-auth-context.tsx` + client-side `useMockAuth`; real Supabase Auth NOT wired. `lib/kudos/actions.ts` uses placeholder `sender_id`. Login uses mock OAuth flow.
- **RLS permissive**: `supabase/migrations/0002_rls_policies.sql` grants anon/auth read-all — not production-hardened.
- Dual Supabase client pattern: `client.ts` (browser, createBrowserClient) + `server.ts` (server actions, createServerClient + cookies).
- **NO CI/CD**: no `.github/workflows/`, no Jenkinsfile, no GitLab CI. No root Dockerfile (ECS module references ECR but no app Dockerfile found at root).
- `.vercel/` present → app likely deployed to Vercel currently, while Terraform provisions a parallel AWS ECS target (deployment-target divergence).
- Locales: vi (default) + en via next-intl.
- Testing: Vitest (unit) + Playwright (14 e2e tests, chromium only).

## Unresolved Questions

- No CI/CD pipeline detected — is deployment manual? Terraform (AWS ECS) vs `.vercel/` (Vercel) suggests two competing deploy targets.
- No root Dockerfile found despite ECS/ECR Fargate infra — container image build path unclear.
- Real authentication integration status (mock vs Supabase Auth) — affects security posture assessment.
